To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

African American doctoral students on a predominately white campus need a mentor/advisor who can help them navigate the culture, politics and socialization process of the predominately White Institution.

(1) the mentor/advisor role is essential to the success for African American students in graduate school, and (2) the mentor/advisors play an important role in the doctoral training and academic success for African Americans in graduate schools.
the African American doctoral experience is unique and the mentor/advisor plays a critical role in the success of the African American student.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mentors/advisers in the doctoral training of African American students.
how African American doctoral students at a predominately White institution are impacted by their mentors and the role they play in the academic success of African American students.
how the mentoring/advisor relationship can be used to help African American doctoral students succeed in their academic endeavors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
African American doctoral students need a strong support system in order to successfully complete their doctoral programs and to become productive members of their respective disciplines.
mentors/advisors play a significant role in the success of the African American student in the doctoral training process.
the mentor/advisor is essential to the success, academic and otherwise, of African American doctoral student at a predominately White Institution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mentor/advisor is an essential component in the success of the African American student in the doctoral program.
the mentor/advisor is a critical component to the success of the African American student in graduate school.

African American doctoral students need to be connected with mentors who have similar backgrounds, and that these mentors should provide a support structure for the African American doctoral candidate to be successful.

the African American doctoral graduate students are in need of more support from their mentor/advisor in the areas of research, teaching, and service.
African American students in doctoral programs need to be connected to a mentor or an advisor that will be supportive of their needs and their goals.
the role of mentors/advisers in the doctoral training of African American students at Predominately white Universities is important.
